problems.title: Median direction in a right triangle
problems.question: The right-angle bisector and hypotenuse median form 25°. Find the larger acute angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: With legs along the axes, the median makes angle theta with one leg, equal to one acute angle; the bisector makes 45°.
steps: |theta−45°|=25°, so theta=20° or 70°. These are the complementary acute angles.

problems.title: When a linear function decreases
problems.question: For which a is y=(a−2)x−3 decreasing?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: A line decreases exactly when its slope is negative.
steps: Require a−2<0, so a<2. The stricter listed conditions a<0 or a<−1 are sufficient subsets but do not give every allowed a.

problems.title: A cube identity disguised by a condition
problems.question: x³−y²=2. Evaluate x⁹−6x³y²−y⁶.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
steps: Put u=x³,v=y², so u−v=2 and 3uv(u−v)=6uv. The expression is therefore (u−v)³=8.

problems.title: Two secants opposite a diameter
problems.question: Two secants meet outside the circle; the farther endpoints form a diameter and the nearer central arc is 48°. Find the exterior angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Exterior secant angle is half the far-arc minus near-arc difference.
steps: The diameter supplies a 180° arc. The angle is (180−48)/2=66°.

problems.title: Two exterior angles determine an inscribed angle
problems.question: In the source figure two exterior secant angles are 28° and 42°. Find the marked top inscribed angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Exterior secant angles equal half their intercepted-arc differences.
steps: Label the circle points T at the top, L left, B bottom, R right. Let u=arc TL+arc TR and v=arc LB+arc BR.
Adding the two exterior-angle relations gives u−v=2(28+42)=140°. Also u+v=360°, so v=110°.
The top angle subtends arc LBR=v, hence is 55°.

problems.title: A tangent-chord angle and a common normal
problems.question: The inner circle in the source diagram touches the outer circle at T and touches the outer diameter line at S. Its tangent-chord angle at S is 68°. O is the outer centre. Find STO.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Tangent-chord theorem; the common tangent at T is perpendicular to OT.
steps: The angle between ST and the tangent at T equals the 68° tangent-chord angle at S.
The radius OT is perpendicular to that tangent, so the marked angle between ST and OT is 90−68=22°.

problems.title: A parallel tangent and a radius crossing a chord
problems.question: In the source diagram AB is parallel to tangent CD at C. OB meets AC at E and AEB=84°. Find the acute angle between AC and the tangent line.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Parallel angles and tangent-chord theorem; OA=OB.
steps: Let BAC=alpha. Because AB is parallel to the tangent at C, the tangent-chord theorem gives ABC=alpha. Thus ACB=180−2alpha.
The centre lies inside the drawn configuration. Triangle OAB has OBA=90−ACB=2alpha−90. Since E lies on BO, ABE has this same angle.
In ABE, alpha+(2alpha−90)+84=180, giving alpha=62°. The marked acute tangent-line angle equals alpha.

problems.title: A base median and a base-vertex bisector
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, the base median and a bisector to an equal side make 70°. Find the apex angle.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The median is perpendicular to the base; the bisector makes half a base angle with it.
steps: If the base angle is beta, 90−beta/2=70, so beta=40°. The apex is 180−2×40=100°.

problems.title: Equivalent equations have the same root
problems.question: For which a are $6(2a-x)-3ax+4=25$ and $0.9x-0.3(2x-1)=3$ equivalent?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Solve the second equation and require the first to have that same unique root.
steps: The second gives 0.3x+0.3=3, hence x=9. Substitution into the first gives −15a−50=25, so a=−5.
The first equation then has nonzero x coefficient 9, so it has exactly that root.

problems.title: Positive integer solutions of a linear equation
problems.question: x,y are positive integers with 3x+7y=23. Find x+y.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Modulo 3, y≡2; positivity gives 1≤y≤2.
steps: Thus y=2 and x=(23−14)/3=3. Their sum is 5.

problems.title: A quadrant missed by a line
problems.question: Which quadrant does y=−1−2x never enter?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Quadrant I requires x>0 and y>0.
steps: For every x>0, y=−1−2x<0, excluding quadrant I. Inputs −1,−1/4,1 produce points in quadrants II,III,IV respectively.

problems.title: A circle centred at a right vertex
problems.question: C is right in ABC, B=33°. The circle centred at C with radius AC meets AB again at D and CB at E. Find AED.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: CA=CD makes CAD isosceles; an inscribed angle is half its central arc.
steps: BAC=57°. Since D lies on AB, CAD=57°, so ACD=180−114=66°.
E lies on the other circle arc, so AED subtends the 66° minor arc AD and equals 33°.

problems.title: A parallel line through a given point
problems.question: The lines y=0.8x+1 and y=kx+b are parallel. The latter passes through (−1.5,−2). Find k+b.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Parallel slopes agree; substitute the point for the intercept.
steps: k=0.8 and −2=0.8(−1.5)+b gives b=−0.8. Their sum is zero.

problems.title: No parameter makes an equation an identity
problems.question: Find a for which $2ax-4a+1=4(ax-1)+2$ has infinitely many solutions.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: An identity needs equal x coefficients and equal constants.
steps: The coefficient condition is 2a=4a, forcing a=0. The constant condition is −4a+1=−2, forcing a=3/4.
They cannot both hold.

problems.title: Flight times with tailwind and headwind
problems.question: The same flight takes 5.5 hours with a 10 km/h tailwind and 6 hours against it. Find the distance.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Ground speeds differ by 20 km/h; speed = distance/time.
steps: For distance D, $D/(11/2)-D/6=20$. The reciprocal difference is 2/11−1/6=1/66.

problems.title: Three arcs on a semicircle over a triangle leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex 72°. A semicircle with an equal side as diameter is divided by the other sides into three arcs. Find the smallest.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Base angles are 54°; an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
steps: Call the diameter AB with apex A. Let D be the intersection with the other equal side, E the intersection with the base. Arc DB is twice A=144°, so arc AD=180−144=36°.
Angle B=54° gives arc AE=108°. Thus arc DE=108−36=72° and arc EB=180−108=72°.
The three arcs are 36°,72°,72°.

problems.title: A parameter makes two equations the same line
problems.question: For which m does $5x+8y=12-mx$, $-x-y=3m-my$ have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Rewrite as $(m+5)x+8y=12$, $-x+(m-1)y=3m$ and require proportional coefficients and constants.
steps: m=0 cannot make proportional constants. For m≠0 the proportionality factor is 4/m.
The y coefficients give $8=(4/m)(m-1)$, so m=−1. At this value the first equation is 4x+8y=12 and the second −x−2y=−3, exactly proportional.

problems.title: Count integer-sided triangles in a small range
problems.question: Count different triangles whose integer side lengths are between 2 and 6 inclusive.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Count sorted triples a≤b≤c with a+b>c; ordering does not produce a new triangle.
steps: Count by the smallest side a. For a=2 the valid counts for b=2,3,4,5,6 are 2,2,2,2,1, totaling 9.
For a=3 the counts for b=3,4,5,6 are 3,3,2,1, totaling 9. For a=4,5,6 the totals are 6,3,1.
The grand total is 9+9+6+3+1=28. Strict inequality excludes degenerate triples such as (2,2,4) and (3,3,6).
problems.note: None of the printed choices (18,9,20,15,22,26) equals the independently enumerated count 28.

problems.title: A factor vanishes under the condition
problems.question: 3x−y=5. Evaluate x²y²−3x³y+5x²y.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Factor the expression as $x^2y(y-3x+5)$.
steps: The condition gives y−3x+5=0. Therefore the whole product is zero.

problems.title: Injectivity of a linear function
problems.question: f(x)=4x−7. Solve f(2x−1)=f(x+5).
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: A nonconstant linear function takes equal values only at equal inputs.
steps: 2x−1=x+5 gives x=6. Substitution into both inputs gives 11.

problems.title: Reciprocals of two roots
problems.question: Find the sum of reciprocals of roots of (2x−1)²=9x².
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Factor using a difference of squares.
steps: (2x−1−3x)(2x−1+3x)=0 gives x=−1 or 1/5. Both are nonzero.
The reciprocal sum is −1+5=4.

problems.title: Solve a reciprocal absolute-value equation
problems.question: Find the larger root of $12/|2x-4|-6.06=-0.06$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Exclude x=2; isolate the reciprocal term.
steps: 12/|2x−4|=6 gives |2x−4|=2. The two roots are x=1 and x=3, both allowed.

problems.title: Two incircle contact points on a rectangle diagonal
problems.question: A rectangle has AB=8,BC=15,AC=17. Incircles of ABC and ACD touch AC at M,N. Find MN.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: The tangent length from a vertex is semiperimeter minus its opposite side.
steps: Both triangles have semiperimeter (8+15+17)/2=20. In ABC, AM=20−15=5.
In ACD, AN=20−8=12. Hence MN=12−5=7.

problems.title: A product that telescopes twice
problems.question: Evaluate $\prod_{k=2}^{199}(1-1/k^2)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
steps: The first product is 1/199; the second is 200/2=100. Their product is 100/199.

problems.title: A prescribed root in an absolute-value equation
problems.question: Find the least positive integer a such that x=3 solves $|3x-2a|-2a+7=1-x$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated geometric or algebraic relation and keep all original restrictions.
formulas: Substitute x=3 and use $|u|=-u$ iff u≤0.
steps: The equation becomes |9−2a|=2a−9=−(9−2a). This holds exactly when 9−2a≤0, or a≥4.5.
The least positive integer is 5.
